:::{#def-product-measure}
#### Product measure

Let $(S, \salg, \measure)$ and $(T, \salgT, \measureb)$ be measure spaces
with [$\sigma$-finite](#def-sigma-finite) measures $\measure$ and $\measureb$.
The **product measure** $\measure \otimes \measureb$
is the measure on the [product $\sigma$-algebra](#def-product-sigma-algebra)
$\salg \otimes \salgT$
that gives each measurable rectangle the product of the measures of its sides:

$$(\measure \otimes \measureb)(A \times B) = \measure(A) \, \measureb(B)
\quad \text{for all } A \in \salg \text{ and } B \in \salgT,$$

with $0 \cdot \infty = \infty \cdot 0 \eqdef 0$
and $x \cdot \infty = \infty \cdot x \eqdef \infty$ for $x > 0$.
Exactly one measure has these values
[@billingsley1995probability, Theorem 18.2].

:::
